x: Davies, Newell and Hallowell led the field after an early dash by Frank Wright. For some unaccountable reason Davies almost stopped with three laps to go and so the race became a duel between Newell and Hallowell.

Pepe started rather fast into the mud while Brian Morris and Frank Wright went off steadily. At the half-way mark Brian was leading slightly from Frank, but Pepe and "Jacko" found the heavy grass track not to their liking and decided to save their energies for the relay.

Our 4 x 110 yds. team failed to materialize and in the 4 x 440 yds. we were fifth. Frank Wright, Pat Fox, Alan Jackson and Brian Morris constituted our team. The medley relay saw us finish in 6th place.

Our own John Davies, Brian Morris, Clive Ryan, Frank Wright and D. McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.

When the first lap time of 54·8 was announced eyebrows were raised and on closer inspection it was seen to be Frank Wright. A barrage of voices carried Frank down the back straight and although caught in the final straight he qualified through second place in 1m.57·2s. - a good solo run.

Whilst talking of half miling we must congratulate Dave Cocks on setting up a new club Junior best of 1:56.4 - a performance which whilst it seemed inevitable, does erase from the book one of the most long-standing club records set up almost ten years ago by Frank Wright.

He bounced back for the road relays in scintillating form, winning our Club youth trial from County Champion Frank Wright and then recording third fastest time of the day in the popular Aylesbury Youth Relay.

Missing information: 800m F.Wright: HJ D.Williams 1.90 (81): LJ C.Brooks 7.06 (71) It is also believed that former Irish International Tony Brien posted marks from 2 Miles upwards that would make the top ten and efforts are being made to trace these performances.
Our Youths performed well in 4th place led home by Frank Wright in 7th. The short road relay season followed the National closely and at Ilford in the 10 x 3½ miles race we entered three teams.
